comment: The command line has to ship with the gem, or `bundle exec git_diff_live` finds nothing in a host app.
Bundler only puts a gem's commands on the path when the gemspec names them.
The engine draws comments, so the store loads with the rest of the library.
A comment is matched to a line by its text, which until now only existed in pieces, as the word-diff segments.
Base and head are checked the same way now, so the check moved into `commit`, shared by both.
The store's own file would show up as a changed file; it is taken out here and its lines handed to the files they are about.

code: | Nothing has changed: #{ @diff.working_tree? ? "the working tree" : @diff.head } matches #{ @diff.base }.
comment: With two commits compared, saying the working tree matches would be wrong.
Comments, the command and two-commit comparison are new features, so this is a minor release with its own entry.

code: - "Whole file" per file, compare from any revision (`main`, `HEAD~3`, a SHA) to the working tree or to another revision, and "Open" to jump to the file in your editor.
comment: The feature list said the page compares with one revision; it now takes two, and comments are the headline addition.

code: | `/changes?base=HEAD~1&head=HEAD` | one commit against another: here, the last commit on its own |
comment: Comparing one commit with the next is how committed comments are read back, so the URL for it is documented with the others.
Where comments are kept and which ones a comparison shows is not guessable from the page, so it is written down here.
There are two skills now, and the new one is meant to run without being asked.

comment: Rebuilt with `rake css`: the bubble column, subgrid rows and field classes are new, and the page ships this file prebuilt.

code: # understands (a SHA, a branch, HEAD~3). +head+ is the commit to compare
comment: The controller's header documents every parameter the page takes; `head` is new.

code: @diff = Diff.new(root: GitDiffLive.configuration.root, base: params[:base].presence || "HEAD", head: params[:head].presence, context: GitDiffLive.configuration.context)
comment: Passes `head` through so `?base=A&head=B` compares two commits, which is how a committed comment is seen again.

code: FIELD = "w-36 px-2 py-1 rounded border border-edge bg-canvas font-mono text-fg placeholder:text-fg-muted focus:outline-none focus:border-accent"
comment: Two text fields now share these classes, so they moved out of the template.
Only a file that has comments gives up width to a fifth column; the others keep the code as wide as before.
Same pattern as the button and link classes: the view asks the helper, and Tailwind finds the classes in this file.
The grid's columns have to be chosen before any row is drawn, from whether a comment has a place in this file.

Rows are grouped from one commented row to the next so each bubble has a block of rows to sit beside, without inline styles or row spans (the host's CSP forbids the first, a prebuilt stylesheet the second).
Agents write names in backticks; drawing them as code keeps a bubble readable without allowing any HTML through.
Links have to keep both ends of the comparison now, so the name no longer says "base".

code: - file_params = { path: file.path, **change_range_params, show: (1 if shown) }.compact
comment: Follows the helper's new name; the file's own links must stay on the same two commits.
Decided once per file: it picks the grid's columns and whether each group gets a comment cell.
Each group is a subgrid on the four code columns with `content-start`, so a bubble taller than its rows leaves the gap under the last row, not between the lines.
Drawn for every group of a commented file, empty or not, so the column reads as one continuous gutter.
Sticky under the file's heading, so the reason stays in view while a long change scrolls past.
With two commits compared there is no working tree or branch to name; the summary names the head instead.
The poll and refresh URLs must carry `head` too, or a live refresh would fall back to the working tree.
"Compare with" had room for one revision. "From ... to" reads correctly with the second field empty (the working tree) or filled.
An agent needs a way to write comments that does not boot Rails or need the server running, hence a plain executable.
Git reports paths from the top of the repository, so the command resolves it and works from any folder.

code: # See Configuration for the options, and Comments for the comments drawn
comment: Points a reader of the module's docs at the new class.
The usage text is the only documentation an agent sees if it runs the command without the skill.
A new 500-line file would spend the agent's context on code it just wrote; it can read numbers off the file instead.
The path is matched lazily up to the first `:+N` or `:-N`, so a path with spaces still parses.
Returns a status instead of exiting, so the tests can run commands in-process against the scratch repository.

code: def changes(paths, base:, all: false, full: false)
comment: A hunk is the unit of "has a comment", not each run of lines: two lines split by one unchanged line are one change to a reader, and listing them apart asked for 61 comments on this very diff.
Unchanged lines inside a hunk are printed without a reference so the agent sees where one run ends and the next begins.
Long lines are cut as well as long runs: a minified stylesheet is one line of 30 kB.
Writes what it can and reports the rest, because resubmitting a batch is safe (a second comment on a line replaces the first).
The anchor is the line's text plus a line-number hint, because numbers shift with every edit above and a bare number would drift onto the wrong line.
The store is a hand-editable, mergeable text file, so a line that is not a comment is skipped rather than breaking the page.
One file for the whole repository keeps a commit's stat to a single extra path; a tree mirroring the source would add a file per file touched.
Every branch appends to the end of the same file, which is a guaranteed conflict on merge without the union driver.
The store would otherwise be listed as a changed file on every page that shows a comment.
Reading the lines the store gained in the diff is what ties a comment to its commit, with no extra git call and no reading of old revisions.
Stale comments are dropped only if written since the base: anything committed earlier is history another comparison still shows.
A wrong line number is the likeliest mistake, so the refusal names the nearest lines that would have worked.
The attributes file is written with the first comment so nobody has to remember to set up the merge driver.
The diff parses the store's patch into comments, so it needs the class.

code: # With a +head+ it compares two commits instead, and the working tree is not
comment: The class comment described a working-tree-only comparison.

code: # +comments+ are the ones written about this file within the comparison,
comment: Each file is handed the comments about it when it is built, so the view never looks anything up.

code: # the files that are no longer the same are drawn again. A new comment
comment: Without the comments in the digest, a newly written comment would not redraw its file on the live page.
Both the page (placing comments) and the command (checking a reference) need the lines a comment may be about.
Matching on text with nearest-number as the tie-break keeps a comment on its line when the file shifts, and drops it when the line is rewritten.
Called for every row drawn, so it returns early for the common file with no comments.

code: @complete ||= self.class.new(root: root, base: base, head: head, context: WHOLE_FILE)
comment: The whole-file view has to compare the same two commits as the page it replaces a file on.
Files and comments both come from the same list now, and the store has to be parsed before the files are built, so the list holds plain attributes rather than finished files.
Returns attributes instead of files so `files` can attach comments at construction.
New features, nothing removed: a minor version.

code: description: Write a one or two sentence comment beside every code change in the working tree saying why it was made. The changes page (git_diff_live) draws each as a bubble next to its code, and they are committed with it. Use when you have finished changing code in a session, before your closing summary, and again after any follow-up change.
comment: The description is what makes an agent run this unprompted, so it says when: after finishing changes, before the summary.

code: Run the commands the way this app runs Bundler.
comment: Comments are written at the end because one written mid-work is dropped as soon as its line is edited again.

code: - **Say why, not what.** The diff already shows what changed. Give the reason: the request, bug, constraint or decision behind it, or what would go wrong without it.
comment: These rules are the ones an agent gets wrong by default: describing the diff, and inventing reasons for changes it did not make.
The cells moved inside a subgrid wrapper, so they are counted there.

code: # Lines 7 to 13: seven rows of four cells.
comment: Same move: the hunk heading is no longer a sibling of the cells.

code: test "compares two commits, leaving the working tree out" do
comment: Covers the new `head` parameter end to end, including that untracked work stays out.

code: test "comments: one is drawn beside the row it was written about, in a column of its own" do
comment: The page-level behaviour of comments: where a bubble is drawn, that other files are untouched, live redraw, and reading one back from a commit.
Same move as above.
Tests write comments through the same class the command uses.
Pins the listing's exact text: it is an interface an agent parses.

code: result = write [ "b_modified.rb", :new, 2, "Tax is part\n  of the total now." ]
comment: Pins the stored format and the anchoring rules: following a shifted line, the nearer of two equal lines, and dropping a rewritten one.
Untracked files belong to the working tree; between two commits there are none, and listing them would show work that is in neither.
